runs.prompt: Ainslie Place gardens, Edinburgh. Standing on the gravel path on the southeast side of the garden's interior oval, looking northwest across the lawn directly at the facade of 7 Ainslie Place. 10am in late October, weather typical for the season.
runs.text:
**Excavation:**

The site is Ainslie Place gardens, a private, key-holder oval garden in the heart of Edinburgh's New Town, part of the Moray Estate development [recall]. The underlying geology is Carboniferous sedimentary rock, shaped by glacial action into the ridges and hollows that define the city's topography [recall]. The garden itself sits within a hollow, surrounded by the imposing Georgian terraces.

The viewpoint is established on the gravel path that circumnavigates the interior oval lawn, specifically on the southeast side [recall]. The camera is at eye level, approximately 1.6 meters above the ground plane (Level 0) [recall]. The sightline is oriented northwest, looking directly across the central lawn [recall].

The target is the facade of 7 Ainslie Place, which stands directly opposite on the northwest side of the oval [recall]. This building is a prime example of Edinburgh's Georgian architecture, constructed c. 1822 as part of the Moray Estate designed by James Gillespie Graham [recall]. It is a multi-story townhouse built of Craigleith sandstone ashlar, featuring a basement area protected by cast-iron railings, a ground floor with a prominent entrance and fanlight, and multiple upper floors with timber sash windows [recall]. The roof is slate with chimney stacks [recall]. The facade is part of a continuous, curved terrace, but 7 Ainslie Place is the central focus of this specific view [recall].

The time is 10am in late October [recall]. The weather is typical for the season in Edinburgh: cool, likely overcast with soft, diffused light, and a damp atmosphere [reach]. The mature deciduous trees within the garden, such as limes and chestnuts, are in full autumn color, with leaves in shades of gold, orange, and brown, many of which have fallen onto the lawn and path [reach]. The gravel path is damp from recent moisture [reach]. The scene is devoid of people and vehicles, emphasizing the quiet, residential character of the private garden and the surrounding architecture [recall].
